_readme: 2026-09-13 SEVEN-REPORT WORKBENCH DECISION: desk CSS ceiling 33600 -> 34000, desk JS 162700 -> 163100 and a separate report-route JS ceiling is introduced at 4000 gzip bytes. Measured bundles are 33890 CSS, 162863 global JS and 3460 report-route JS. The presentation gives General Ledger, Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, VAT Summary, Stock Balance, Rent Roll and Owner Ledger one compact scope summary, persistent recoverable request state, explicit empty-state action, semantic total/section bands and bidi-isolated numeric values. Frappe preloads query-report, so page_js cannot deliver an app Page script there; the global bundle carries only a query-report route loader and fetches the hashed workbench on demand, while that workbench activates only for the seven named reports. The workbench delegates to the live throttled refresh; native filters, prepared reports, virtualization, sort state and export payload remain untouched. A containing-block correction also confines Frappe's transparent onboarding layer to its sidebar instead of letting it intercept the entire page. No dependency, query, calculation, permission bypass or parallel report controller was added.

2026-09-13 RECOVERABLE LIST REFRESH DECISION: desk CSS ceiling 33500 -> 33600 gzip bytes and JS ceiling 161600 -> 162700 gzip bytes. Final measured bundles are 33539 CSS and 162700 JS. The growth adds one in-context role=alert state around each live Frappe list instance's native refresh Promise, a labelled keyboard-focusable Retry action, Arabic copy, responsive presentation and a lazy-load-safe installer. Retry calls the original bound refresh after clearing only the failed request throttle; native filters, saved views, paging, selection, permissions and rendered rows remain Frappe-owned. No dependency, endpoint, query, prototype-wide patch, parallel list controller or data model was added.

2026-09-07 RAIL HOVER TRIGGER DECISION: desk JS ceiling 152600 -> 153100 gzip bytes. Actual JS grows 152600 -> 153014 (+414) to WIRE A TRIGGER THAT WAS WRITTEN AND READ BY NOTHING. `data-bnd-sb-railtrigger` carries the Theme Settings choice (Hover / Click / Hover + Pin) and was set on <html> at apply_sidebar_attrs, but no listener ever consumed it -- grep for mouseenter/mouseleave/pointerenter across bunood.js returned ZERO matches -- so a desk set to Hover could only expand through the toggle button. Measured on the live desk before the change: data-bnd-rail present, trigger 'hover', pointer held over the pane for 1.2s, `bnd-rail-open` never added and the pane stayed at 96px; forcing the class widened it to 280px, proving _sidebar-layout.scss:57 was correct all along and only the gesture was absent. The bytes are mouseenter/mouseleave/focusin/focusout handlers with their guards (narrow, customize mode, pinned, and 'focus is inside so closing would strand it'), a (hover: hover) gate so coarse pointers keep the toggle, and the Hover + Pin click. The pin reuses `bnd-rail-pinned`, a class already in sb_teardown_rail's remove() list that nothing set -- so that teardown line becomes honest and no teardown change was needed. No dependency or duplicate control was added; other ceilings and release history are unchanged.

2026-09-07 SWITCHER DEDUPE DECISION: desk JS ceiling 152410 -> 152600 gzip bytes. Actual JS grows 152410 -> 152505 (+95) to repair the pane-head switcher's duplicate Home row. The dedupe set was built from __() LABELS while the filter tests w.title, the English name Frappe stores, so the two sides could only ever match on an ENGLISH desk: in Arabic `taken` held الصفحة الرئيسية, w.title was Home, nothing was dropped and the switcher rendered Home twice (user-reported, with a screenshot). The fix carries an untranslated `key` on the two action rows and matches on that. A first draft cost +285 because the argument was written at the call site and build.mjs ships this file verbatim; the prose was cut to a pointer, which is the 190 bytes that came back. No dependency, router or duplicate control was added; other ceilings and release history are unchanged.

The payload budget (GUIDELINES §2.5). `ceiling` is a HARD gate on the
built bundle's gzip bytes — tools/payload.mjs --check fails when the
build crosses it, and the suite runs that check on every verify.
Raising a ceiling is a DECISION: edit the number in the same commit
as the change that needs it, and say why in that commit's message.
`history` is the per-release record — append with
`node tools/payload.mjs --record vX.Y.Z` at tag time. Raw bytes are
recorded for parse-cost context; the ceiling is gzip because the wire
is what a first paint waits on.

the account band and panel: the pane's foot becomes ONE toolbar of

AND css -> 22300 closing item 40's last filed defect: the brand pane's
Glass rebuilds its gradient with the transparency mixed into each stop,

(bnd_own panetoggle, stamped only after the trigger wiring is live).

AND -> 106500 for slice 13, the user's two picks: the badge roll-up (a

AND TO 102600 for slice 8d, drag-to-resize — the survey's clearest
differentiator (every product tool has it, no ERP surveyed does, and

RAISED AGAIN TO 99450 for slice 8: the in-pane filter (the survey's clearest
gap — 6/13 product tools have one, 0/14 ERPs — and ERPs are the ones with

98800 was the first number and it was nine bytes too tight: the retry that
mounts the head has to RE-CHECK ITS OWN PREMISE, because it outlives the
call that scheduled it and a pending attempt otherwise lands after the
teardown. That is a correctness line, not a comment, so the ceiling moved
rather than the code.
Ceilings start at ~15% over the v0.12.0 measurement — headroom for a
normal slice, tight enough that a dependency or a generated blob
cannot slip in unnoticed.
SEPARATE CEILINGS, NOT A SUM (item 32; count-free since item 35 — the count drifted twice). `css_gzip` is the desk bundle, which
only an authenticated desk fetches; `web_css_gzip` is bunood-web.<hash>.css,
which every WEBSITE page fetches. They are never both on one page, so summing
them would bound a number nobody pays — and would break every history row's
comparability at the release that introduced the second sheet. Rows before
v0.32.0 carry no web_css_* keys because the file did not exist; that is the
honest shape, not a gap.
THAT SECOND SENTENCE USED TO READ 'the login sheet, which only a logged-out
visitor fetches', and item 33 made it false in the same release that made it
matter: the sheet now loads on every public page, every portal page and every
web form, for signed-in and signed-out visitors alike. The audience for these
bytes went from two routes to the whole website, so the ceiling is now the
tightest one here in practice even though it is the smallest number.
RAISED 98200 -> 98300 by item 40's ownership repair (2026-08-30). The repair is
~40 gzip bytes of runtime: `claim_panehead`, one entry in remount_chrome's
disown list, and a build-only branch in sb_mount_brand. It cost more at first
draft -- 449 bytes -- because the ARGUMENT was written at the JS call sites,
and build.mjs copies that file verbatim by policy, so every comment ships. The
prose moved to _layouts.scss, where Sass strips `//` before the wire and where
the ownership contract already lived. What is left is the feature. Item 40's
slice 4 is a deletion slice and is expected to return this and more; if it does
not, this number should come back down rather than stay as headroom.
tools/payload.mjs THROWS on any dist file that matches no bucket, so a
third entry cannot repeat item 32's near-miss of shipping unmeasured.

AND TO 109800 for the account band's repair. 42 bytes: one SB_PARTS row
(`tenants`), one deleted line in the utils teardown, and two pointer comments --

are the placed tenants. So ONE `sb_apply` -- a settings click, the start button,
or the pill's way back -- took the bell and the account out of the DOM and nothing
put them back: a Unified Side Pane desk with no route to Log Out until reload.
Measured on a live desk, and found by the matrix's new pane-state axis.
AND TO 110000 for `retire()`, which stops a DEAD CHART from redrawing on every
window resize. frappe-charts binds one window `resize` listener per instance and
removes it nowhere; when Frappe re-renders the widget the chart lived in, the
object survives with a detached container and the next resize calls
`makeChartArea`, whose first act is `this.container.removeChild(this.svg)` -- and
that throws. Three full-run gates recorded it as an unexplained pageerror in
`desk.bundle.js` that no isolated reproduction could source. We already track live
charts and already prune the dead ones; pruning only stopped US redrawing them.
81 bytes unbinds the vendor's listener too, and the argument went to
surfaces/_charts.scss where Sass strips it.
AND css_gzip TO 22900 for v0.42.1, the pane seen: +184 gzip. The rail rest state
gained a SECOND ARM -- Frappe own collapse, `.body-sidebar-container:not(.expanded)`,
which no rule had ever styled and which is the 50px pane with one-letter labels the
user photographed -- so every rest rule now compiles to two long selectors. The
page-head brand (the pill replacement) and the search bar are the rest. The
shortcuts block (96 lines) came out in the same commit, which is why +184 and not
+400. Growth is the two-arm rest state; it is the feature.
